reviews.title: Good but missing key features
reviews.text:
As a personal trainer and physical therapist, this is one of the best workout logging apps I’ve used (and I’ve used a lot). I have been overall pleased with the coaching feature. Only making adjustments for available equipment most weeks. Will say the progression doesn’t always recognize when an exercise is harder to progress safely so follow the coach weight with caution if it feels like a large weight increase. 

I love the body map and the way it keeps track of PR. Good for motivating you and the insights are nice too. 

Things to improve: rest timers!! They turn off constantly for no reason. I have to turn them back on every workout because I swapped an exercise or something totally unrelated. 
Also time. There’s no option to switch reps to time for exercises like plank or farmers walk. Also no choice to pick body weight instead for things like pull-ups unless the exercise was preset to body weight. 

Also leg press machine in specific has crazy low numbers and my weight class is world class at an extremely low weight despite being more reasonable on squat for example. 

Overall though I’m motivated and more accountable. Will continue to use. Worth the subscription.

reviews.title: Amazing app!!! Minor bugs
reviews.text: I love this app. Has been so helpful to plan my workouts and to track progress really easily. It does have several non-important bugs and things that could be improved with the UI. But nothing that outweighs how great this app has been to use. It is paid but its super cheap. The year plan was something like $3 a month. Lets be honest, that's not even half the price of a coffee. I do hope one day they update a few more things on it but for now I love the app.

reviews.title: Love this app! A few ideas to improve:
reviews.text:
First off this app is amazing highly recommend! They’re quick to add new workouts and seem to be constantly improving the app so I’m excited to see where it goes! I got my friend into it and it really motivates us to go harder and I don’t know if I’d be as consistent without this app, honestly! 

I’d LOVE if they optimized it for yoga/stretching as well. Track flexibility scores by how long we hold various stretches and as we work to more advanced ones. 

I’d also love if cardio was muscle group or had its own score system as well so I can better track my cardio progress (the app has already made some improvements on this with having timers for treadmill but I’d like it to have a score like my other muscles) 

These changes would bring this app to a 5 star rating for me.

reviews.title: Great app, still buggy
reviews.text: Overall, I’ve been really enjoying this app as a way to design and track my workouts. I like that it’s focused only on weight lifting. However, the AI-coach feature is still incredibly buggy. I tried using it to design the 6-week routine with 5x workouts a week, and I think if you happen to skip a day, it starts acting weird. It had me doing the routine on a Tues->Tues cycle instead of Mon->Mon, which was confusing. Also it gives you a deload week but then it essentially resets all your progress and you lose strength points for it. At one point I tried to reset the whole thing and even when it said “pull day” with back and biceps exercises listed, when I clicked to start, it still had the old leg day exercises. The coach feature is a great idea but needs a lot of work.

reviews.title: Perfect app for the gym, very beginner friendly!
reviews.text:
I love this app, perfect for personalizing and keeping all my different machine weights logged for me so I don’t have to worry about it. When I first started attending the gym I tried making an excel spreadsheet to help me track my machine weights but this app does it for me and really makes it fun to see which muscle groups I focus on more then others. The couch tips are super helpful and have been a game changer for me in form and weight level.

I do wish it was a little cheaper price-wise ($9.99 per month) but I definitely do recommend this app to all gym goers. I recommend at least trying it out for a month before deciding if it’s the app for you and your gym style.
